title: Control plane: Dedicated rollout plan CRUD APIs + validation + basic RBAC
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Implements CRUD for Dedicated staged rollout plans in the control plane service, including server-side validation and basic RBAC enforcement.

Context
- This builds on pr-28411 (DB schema + migrations). This PR wires the schema into the service and exposes initial endpoints so Console + operators can create/update/get/list plans.
- Promote/abort + audit events are intentionally out of scope here (tracked in pr-28458).

What’s included
- API surface (internal + Console backend use)
  - POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans
  - GET  /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}
  - GET  /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans (supports filtering by status + pagination)
  - PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id} (draft-only updates)
- Validation rules (enforced on create + update)
  - stage monotonicity: stages must be strictly increasing by allocation (traffic_pct or replica_count depending on stage.mode)
  - uniqueness: stage IDs + names unique within a plan
  - minimum headroom guardrail: ensure smallest stage alloc does not violate pool-level min canary size and headroom requirements
  - multi-region constraint: if pool has multiple regions, stage definitions must be compatible across regions (no per-region allocation yet)
  - draft immutability rules: once a plan is RUNNING, stage definitions are immutable (only metadata fields allowed)
- Basic RBAC
  - Read access: any principal with pool read access (customer admin + internal)
  - Write access (create/update): requires dedicated_pool_rollout:write permission
  - Enforcement is via authz middleware + explicit permission checks at handler level (defense-in-depth).
  - Adds temporary feature flag guard (dedicated_staged_rollouts) to block plan creation unless enabled for the account/pool.

Not included / follow-ups
- promote/abort/hold state machine actions and idempotency keys (pr-28458)
- audit event emission for CRUD actions (security requested; we’ll add once the audit schema lands; tracked under ENG-5932 subtasks)
- gate evaluation / policy engine integration (pr-28476)

Testing
- Unit tests for validation edge cases: decreasing stages, zero/negative allocations, duplicate IDs, and draft-only update enforcement
- API handler tests: RBAC deny cases, feature flag deny, pagination/filters
- Manual: used dev console to create a plan against a staging Dedicated pool; verified list/get responses and update constraints

Docs
- Added OpenAPI snippets + examples for Console backend integration

Rollout
- Safe to ship behind dedicated_staged_rollouts flag. No behavior changes for existing customers without the flag.

Screenshots/Examples
- Example create request:
  { "name": "mistral-7b-v2 rollout", "stages": [{"id":"canary","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":1},{"id":"ramp","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":10},{"id":"full","mode":"traffic_pct","allocation":100}] }
- Example validation error:
  "stages must be strictly increasing: stage 'ramp' allocation=10 must be > previous stage 'canary' allocation=10"
commits: validation: stage monotonicity + allocation bounds + uniqueness checks
rbac: permission gate for rollout plan writes + feature flag guard
api: add pagination/filter support to list endpoint
tests: handler authz cases + validation edge cases
review_conversation: 2025-02-19 Ethan Park: Looks good overall. Two concerns: (1) update endpoint should be draft-only, and (2) list endpoint needs pagination to avoid huge payloads for noisy customers. Can we enforce both now?
2025-02-19 Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. I’ll enforce draft-only updates (return 409 with current status) and add cursor-based pagination (limit default 50).

2025-02-20 Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC: please avoid relying only on middleware. I’d like explicit permission checks in the handlers as well. Also confirm that customer admins can read but cannot create without rollout write permission.
2025-02-20 Benji Okafor (author): Done. Added explicit requirePermission('dedicated_pool_rollout:write') in create/update. Read remains pool-read. Added tests for both deny cases.

2025-02-21 Jordan Lee: Validation: monotonicity check should allow mixed modes or not? If stage.mode can differ per stage, monotonicity gets ambiguous. We should either forbid mixed mode or define ordering semantics.
2025-02-21 Benji Okafor (author): For v1, I’m forbidding mixed mode within a plan. Added validation: all stages must share a single mode. Added clear error message + tests.
2025-02-22 Chloe Martin: Console backend expects list endpoint to support filtering by status and include 'current_stage' when running. Can we include the field even if it’s null for draft?
2025-02-22 Benji Okafor (author): Added status filter and included current_stage (nullable). Also added 'last_updated_by' for better UI strings.

2025-02-23 Ethan Park: One more nit: min headroom guardrail should be computed using pool size *and* min_canary_replicas. The current code only checks percent. Please align with infra guidelines (small pools).

2025-02-23 Benji Okafor (author): Updated to compute effective canary allocation by mode, with a minimum replica floor. If the pool is too small, we fail validation with a suggested stage set (1/10/100 -> 1/100).

2025-02-24 Kaitlyn Nguyen: Approving with the note that we still need audit events for CRUD for enterprise change management. Please make sure follow-up PR includes create/update events too (not only promote/abort).
2025-02-24 Benji Okafor (author): Ack. Added a TODO + linked in ENG-5932 subtasks; we’ll emit audit events once schema is finalized.
2025-02-24 Jordan Lee: Approved. Thanks for tightening mixed-mode semantics; that will simplify gate evaluation integration later.
2025-02-24 Ethan Park: Approved. Pagination + draft-only update make this safe to expose behind the feature flag.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Ethan Park into main
release_notes: Adds initial control plane CRUD APIs for Dedicated staged rollout plans (create/get/list/update) behind dedicated_staged_rollouts feature flag.
Enforces stage validation guardrails (monotonicity, uniqueness, min headroom) and basic RBAC for write operations.
